title: Brain organoids: Experimental access to human-specific brain development
title_zh: 脑类器官：实验获取人类特异性大脑发育的方法
abstract: Human cerebral cortical development includes species-divergent cellular programs and unusually prolonged trajectories that remain difficult to investigate experimentally. These processes support human-specific cognitive abilities and are thought to be associated with vulnerability to neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders. Human brain organoids provide a tractable system for studying these processes across developmental time and under controlled perturbation. Here, we review how cortical organoids model human-specific features of progenitor biology and cell diversification, as well as progressive cellular maturation and circuit formation. We consider the limitations that constrain later-stage maturation and how approaches including the addition of missing cell types, the use of assembloids, and transplantation can extend the developmental processes accessible to study. Finally, we examine how patient-derived, isogenic, chimeric, and perturbation-based organoid systems are being used to investigate neurodevelopmental disorders and, in turn, reveal mechanisms of typical human development.
abstract_zh: 人类大脑皮层发育包括具有物种差异的细胞程序和异常延长的发育轨迹，这些过程在实验上仍难以研究。这些过程支撑着人类特异的认知能力，并被认为与神经发育障碍和神经精神障碍的易感性相关。人类脑类器官为在发育时间上以及可控干扰条件下研究这些过程提供了可行的体系。在这里，我们综述了皮层类器官如何模拟人类特异的祖细胞生物学和细胞分化，以及渐进的细胞成熟和电路形成。我们考虑限制后期成熟的局限性，以及包括添加缺失细胞类型、使用类器官簇（assembloids）和移植在内的方法如何扩展可供研究的发育过程。最后，我们探讨了患者来源的、同源的、嵌合的和基于干扰的类器官系统如何被用于研究神经发育障碍，进而揭示典型人类发育的机制。
